Gera
GHEE-ruh
proper noun
Hebrew Gera, perhaps “a grain” or “sojourning,” an ancestral name in the tribe of Benjamin.

📖 Biblical Definition

Gera was a name borne in the tribe of Benjamin from its earliest generations, for Gera is numbered among the sons of Benjamin who went down into Egypt (Gen 46:21), and the name recurs in the genealogies of the tribe (1Ch 8:3, 5, 7). Two famous Benjamites are called sons of Gera, and they stand in sharpest contrast. The first is Ehud the son of Gera, the left-handed deliverer whom the LORD raised up when Israel cried unto Him under the oppression of Eglon king of Moab; Ehud slew the tyrant and freed the land, and it had rest fourscore years (Judg 3:15). The second is Shimei the son of Gera, the man of the house of Saul who came forth cursing as David fled from Absalom, casting stones and dust at the LORD’s anointed in the day of his affliction (2Sa 16:5). Thus the one name of Gera was father to a deliverer and to a reviler, to a man who saved Israel and a man who cursed her king. Gera stands as a witness that a single house may bring forth both the faithful and the faithless, and that men are not measured by the name they inherit but by the heart they bear before the LORD.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Benjamite ancestral name; father of Ehud the deliverer and of Shimei who cursed David.

GERA, an ancestral name in the tribe of Benjamin.

Gera was among the sons of Benjamin who came into Egypt (Gen 46:21).

Ehud the son of Gera was the deliverer who slew Eglon of Moab (Judg 3:15).

Shimei the son of Gera cursed David in his flight (2Sa 16:5).

The name recurs in the genealogies of Benjamin (1Ch 8:3).

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 46:21 — "And the sons of Benjamin were Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard."

Judg 3:15 — "But when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded: and by him the children of Israel sent a present unto Eglon the king of Moab."

2Sa 16:5 — "And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came."

1Ch 8:3 — "And the sons of Bela were, Addar, and Gera, and Abihud,"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; the name witnesses that one house may bring forth both the faithful and the faithless.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the contrast of the two sons of Gera. From the one Benjamite name came Ehud, a deliverer raised up by the LORD to free Israel, and Shimei, a reviler who cursed the LORD’s anointed in his affliction. A single house may bring forth both the faithful and the faithless; men are not measured by the name they inherit but by the heart they bear before God.

Gera’s line also illustrates how the same tribe and stock may serve very different ends in the providence of God. Benjamin gave Israel both her first king and her great deliverers, and also some of her bitterest opponents of the throne of David. The diversity within one house is a standing rebuke to all confidence in lineage; grace is not hereditary, and each generation must turn to the LORD for itself.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name perhaps means “a grain” or “sojourning,” an old Benjamite name of several bearers.

Gera — Hebrew Gera, perhaps “a grain” or “sojourning.”

It was among the names of the sons of Benjamin.

Ehud the deliverer was called the son of Gera.

Shimei the reviler was also called the son of Gera.

The one name fathered both a deliverer and a curser.
